evals.title: Collective credit and calibrated causality
evidence: Fresh read-only execution of `node scripts/run-knowledge-development.mjs` recomputed the exact candidate fingerprint `5c1ab3d7743e8764a33b7288bf2a188b347fd139986315fa74876aea5af74a34` and reported four KC Town Hall funding sources, two claims, and zero validation errors.

`apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:169-248` decomposes the evidence into five observations: City-listed developer/presenter, CCED Board recommendation, Council acceptance plus negotiation authority, Council appropriation, and 2024 withdrawal plus unused-funds reappropriation. The limitations explicitly distinguish recommendation from appropriation, negotiation from execution or receipt, and appropriation from payment, expenditure, or completion.

`apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:251-385` keeps `CLM-KCTH-CCED-DEVELOPER-PRESENTER-ROLE` separate from `CLM-KCTH-CCED-COUNCIL-FUNDING-CHAIN`. Its active funding projection says, “This was authorization, not receipt: KC Town Hall later withdrew, and in 2024 the Council reappropriated the unused $490,539,” while its boundaries require that ending whenever the appropriation is presented and reject claims that Jamie “secured or caused” it.

`apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:3-41` renders the role and funding chronology as separate Claim occurrences, states that the designation does not turn government decisions into Jamie's accomplishment, and explicitly distinguishes recommendation, acceptance, appropriation, agreement, payment, receipt, expenditure, and completion.

`apps/www/src/data/work.ts:529-595` keeps collaborator credit, the unused-funds ending, and the prohibition on describing the money as received or spent in the card summary, status, evidence, and Known/Open/Protected fields.

Existing collective-credit records retain the same calibration: `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/development-records.ts:487-517` preserves Suzanne Hogan, participant, housemate, and communal-governance credit; `development-records.ts:606-624` preserves the multi-group Cabaret campaign and named government actors; and `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/nycac-research-2026-07-14.ts:604-656` separates Jamie's testimony from Council enactment and the City's later replacement of MARCH.

Fresh targeted verification passed both KC Town Hall tests in `scripts/tests/knowledge-development-evals.test.mjs:223-304` with zero failures. `npm run check:citations` also passed canonical-record, public-projection, boundary, and page-plan consistency.
evals.recommended_next_move: Preserve the current role-versus-government-decision decomposition, mandatory unused-funds ending, and regression coverage; no material revision is needed.

evals.title: Source-backed strength through Chad's lens
evidence: `apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:18-45` is concise and professionally organized around what became usable, Jamie's work, the official funding record, and transferable implementation proof; it does not expose the underlying registry machinery.

`apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:251-336` strengthens the case with the exact City-listed developer/presenter role and a precise official chronology without converting Board or Council action into Jamie's impact.

`apps/www/src/data/work.ts:529-595` directly names the role, planning and documentation outputs, municipal source map, collaborator credit, implementation fit, withdrawal, and reappropriation. The ending is stated matter-of-factly without blame or language that negates the demonstrated work.

Selection is purposeful: `apps/www/src/data/work.ts:537-540` keeps the short proof non-featured at priority 6; `docs/knowledge-bank/promotion-slate.md:28-36` selects only the bounded role and funding-chain claims; and `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/records.ts:784-811` defines only those two claim occurrences for the public page.

The concise Technical Operations projection uses the bounded wording “Presented an adaptive-reuse proposal that advanced through CCED and Council review” through `apps/www/src/data/proofs.ts:528-545` and `apps/www/src/app/work/technical-operations/page.tsx:142-159`, rather than dumping the full chronology or source registry.
findings: The official records atomically establish Jamie's developer/presenter designation and the governmental chronology, but the broader public assertions that Jamie “helped shape redevelopment planning, public-benefit documentation, stakeholder context, and municipal-review support” and made materials usable to collaborators (`apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:18-24`) rely only on the broad approved-resume/public-safe-summary source basis in `apps/www/src/data/proofs.ts:528-545`. No KC-specific atomic observation identifies Jamie's division of that work or a concrete collaborator-use instance, preventing a fully source-backed score of 4.
evals.recommended_next_move: Add one public-safe atomic observation, artifact, or concrete use example tying Jamie specifically to the planning/documentation work and showing how a collaborator used it; retain the present official chronology and candid ending unchanged.
